11.4a — MC Strategy + Practice Set 1

70 questions, 120 minutes — about 100 seconds each, no penalty for guessing. Today is not about learning new content; it is about a STRATEGY for a 2-hour sprint, plus your first full-conditions practice set. Read the strategy guide first.

Strategy ~15 min

The three-pass method:

  1. Pass 1 (about 80 min): answer every question you know instantly. Flag the rest — NO lingering. A skipped question costs ~100 seconds; a lingered one costs 300 and steals the same points from later questions
  2. Pass 2 (about 30 min): the flagged ones you can eliminate on. Wrong answers have TELLS — read them before solving
  3. Pass 3 (about 10 min): what remains. Answer EVERYTHING. No penalty = guessing is free points; an empty bubble is the only wrong choice

Wrong-answer tells you already know from this class:

  • Off-by-one options (loop runs n vs n-1 times — the exam builds distractors from off-by-one mistakes)
  • "Always/never" absolutes (rarely true — the world runs on tradeoffs, 9.3)
  • Right answer with wrong REASON (two options say "10"; only one says why) — the "why" options test whether you traced the code or guessed the number
  • Binary/hex conversion options with transposed digits (9.2's 0x1F vs 0xF1 — they KNEW that was your error)

Socratic

The MC section includes some questions about "innovations' impacts" (IOC-1) with no code in them. Where does the time you save by bubbling fast on tracing questions go — and why is a 100-second average a LIE (some questions need 30s, some need 180)?

Practice Set 115 questions, 15 min

15 questions in 15 minutes. Mixed across the ten CED families. Answer every question — there is no penalty for guessing, and a blank scores like a wrong one. When the timer stops, press Grade this set for your scorecard and the family error table.

1. A newspaper reports that "62% of Americans support the new policy," based on a survey of 1,000 people recruited through one website's opt-in poll. What is the most significant limitation of this conclusion?DAT-2

2. What is displayed after this code runs?AAP-1

a ← 5
b ← 2
result ← a / b
DISPLAY(result)

3. What is the value of result?AAP-2

result ← MOD(17, 5)

4. Two procedures are written. Which statement best explains why double is preferred over doubleFive?AAP-3

PROCEDURE doubleFive()
{
    RETURN 5 * 2
}

PROCEDURE double(n)
{
    RETURN n * 2
}

5. How many times does the body of the loop run?AAP-2

count ← 0
REPEAT UNTIL (count = 6)
{
    count ← count + 2
}

6. A list holds the values shown. What does the code display?AAP-2

aList ← [10, 20, 30]
REMOVE(aList, 1)
DISPLAY(aList)

7. A user complains that a video call stutters and freezes even though their internet plan advertises very high download speed. Their speed test confirms the high number. Which explanation best fits?CSN-1

8. A large website stores identical copies of every page on servers in three different regions, and DNS can return any of them. What does this design primarily provide?CSN-1

9. A program must assign a unique ID to each of 40 students. What is the minimum number of bits required per ID?DAT-1

10. A photographer must choose a format for a portfolio that will be printed at full size. Which statement about the two formats is accurate?DAT-1

11. A photo taken on a phone includes the date, time, GPS coordinates, and camera model even though none of that is visible in the image. What is this information called?DAT-2

12. A neighborhood association uses a mapping tool to record potholes. Residents submit photos with location data. A researcher then uses the map to report which neighborhoods receive the slowest repairs. Which concern is most directly raised?IOC-1

13. Which of the following is the clearest example of personally identifiable information (PII)?IOC-1

14. A message claims to be from a bank and asks the recipient to click a link and "confirm your account password because of a security update." A second message spreads itself to every contact in a victim's address book without the victim's knowledge. Which terms best describe the two?IOC-1

15. A student finds a JavaScript function on a public code-sharing site and uses it in a school project, changing variable names. What is the correct approach under the College Board's collaboration and citation rules?CRD-1

Error Table & Debrief ~15 min

The scorecard matters more than the score. Grading gives you the raw numbers automatically; the work is what you do with them. Copy the scorecard's family table into your error table and add the two columns the machine cannot see — your time (instant / eliminator / guess) and the misconception sentence for every miss. Which FAMILY bleeds points decides your homework, and the next two classes target it (11.4b data and networks, 11.4c algorithms and systems).

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain the three-pass method and the 100-second average's lie
  • Name three wrong-answer tells and spot them in Set 1
  • Show your error table with families and times
  • Have a study plan targeting your weakest family
